content: [{"id": "hdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Communications", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "WhatsApp Accounts", "col": 4}}, {"id": "sc3", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Push Settings", "col": 4}}, {"id": "shortcutNotifSettings", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Notification Settings", "col": 4}}, {"id": "sc4", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Call Log", "col": 6}}, {"id": "sc5", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "WhatsApp Messages", "col": 6}}, {"id": "telhdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Telephony Setup", "col": 12}}, {"id": "telintro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Four steps, in order. Every provider names these differently — Acefone calls a number a My Number, Ozonetel calls it a Virtual Number — but they are the same four things, so a new provider reuses this screen.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tel1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Telephony Account — one per provider tenant. Its webhook token is what authenticates the provider; HMAC and an IP allowlist are optional and off until you turn them on.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tel2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Numbers (DIDs) — one row per number the business gives you, and the grain it belongs to. A number that is not listed here is dropped. That is what keeps other businesses off a shared provider account out of this CRM. Type the number; pick the grain — it must match the grain on the leads, or a call attaches to nothing.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tel3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Agents — only for agents whose provider email is not their CRM login. Staff whose email matches a CRM user resolve on their own and need no row. An unmapped agent never costs you the call; it only leaves the rep blank.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tel4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Capture Rules — inside Telephony Settings. Which calls become Call Logs, by direction and channel. Empty captures nothing; telephony is on once you add a rule.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "telafter", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Every delivery is logged either way. A call that is dropped or declined is recorded in Integration Request with the reason — fix the reason, replay the row, and the call lands.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "telsc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Telephony Accounts", "col": 3}}, {"id": "telsc2", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Telephony Routing", "col": 3}}, {"id": "telsc3", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "User Mapping", "col": 3}}, {"id": "telsc4", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Capture Rules", "col": 3}}, {"id": "fbhdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Facebook Routing", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fbintro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Four steps, in order. A Facebook form collects whatever the campaign asked for; this decides which of those answers become a lead, and which business line that lead belongs to. Nothing arrives until the last step is taken — a source is dormant when it is created.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fb1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Contract — the grain every lead from this form is stamped with, and the field list the form is allowed to write. It is chosen once, on the source. A source cannot be enabled without one, because a lead with no grain is owned by nobody and routed by no rule.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fb2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Lead Sync Source — one per form being crawled, holding the Page access token. The Pages and their lead forms are discovered and stored when it is saved, so the token is exercised immediately: if it cannot see the Business that owns the Page, it is refused here rather than months later in silence.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fb3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Field Mapping — on the Facebook Lead Form, each question is pointed at a CRM field. The list offered is exactly what the contract allows for that grain, so a field outside it cannot be chosen. An unmapped question is collected and discarded — the answer reaches Facebook and stops there. Phone is required: the lead is deduped on it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fb4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Enable & frequency — how often the form is crawled. Only leads created since the last successful crawl are fetched, so an hourly form and a daily form cost the same. This is the switch that starts everything; until it is set, the source is configured and idle.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fbafter", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Every refusal is recorded in Failed Lead Sync Log with its reason. Two are worth watching: Duplicate is ordinary — the same Facebook lead was already taken. Unconfigured Form is not: it means the form this source points at is no longer one Facebook reports for the Page, which happens when a form is duplicated or rebuilt and takes a new id. The source keeps crawling a form that no longer exists and returns nothing, so it is named here instead of passing as a quiet day.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fbsc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Lead Sync Sources", "col": 3}}, {"id": "fbsc2", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Facebook Lead Forms", "col": 3}}, {"id": "fbsc3", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Facebook Settings", "col": 3}}, {"id": "fbsc4", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Lead Sync Failures", "col": 3}}]
